types.oie_definition: The title of a film or movie.
types.embedding_query_text: Movie Title: The title of a film or movie. Also called Film Title, Movie Name, Cinema Title.

candidates.label: Movie
candidates.comment: A creative work that is a motion picture film. Also called film, motion picture, cinema. Examples: "The Shawshank Redemption", "Avatar", "Parasite", "Casablanca". Distinct from TVSeries, which is a collection of episodes.

candidates.label: MovieTheater
candidates.comment: A MovieTheater is a civic structure designed for public viewing of movies. Also called cinema, picture house, movie house. Examples: AMC Theatres, local independent cinema, drive-in movie theater. Distinct from MovieRentalStore, which is a business for renting movies.

candidates.label: MovieClip
candidates.comment: A MovieClip, as a CreativeWork Clip, is a short segment or part of a movie. Also called film clip, video clip, movie segment, film segment. Examples: a movie trailer, a deleted scene, a blooper reel, a short excerpt used in a review. Distinct from MovieSeries, which is a collection of related films.

candidates.label: ScreeningEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving the public showing of a movie or other video content. Also called film screening, movie showing, video presentation, cinema event. Examples: a film festival screening, a premiere showing of a new movie, a public documentary viewing, a drive-in movie night.

candidates.label: MovieRentalStore
candidates.comment: A MovieRentalStore is a local business that offers movies for rent. Also called video rental store, film rental shop, DVD rental store. Examples: Blockbuster (historical), local video rental shop, Redbox kiosk. Distinct from MovieTheater, which is a venue for viewing movies.

types.oie_definition: A specific point in time, typically represented in a day-month-year or year-month-day format.
types.embedding_query_text: Date: A specific point in time, typically represented in a day-month-year or year-month-day format. Also called Day, Calendar Date, Timestamp.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

types.oie_definition: The amount of money earned by a movie or film at the box office.
types.embedding_query_text: Box Office Figure: The amount of money earned by a movie or film at the box office. Also called Box Office Revenue, Movie Earnings, Film Revenue.

chosen_type.label: BoxOfficeFigure
chosen_type.definition: The amount of money earned by a movie or film at the box office.
chosen_type.justification: No existing type specifically represents box office figures

candidates.comment: A creative work that is a motion picture film. Also called film, motion picture, cinema. Examples: "The Shawshank Redemption", "Avatar", "Parasite", "Casablanca". Distinct from TVSeries, which is a collection of episodes.

candidates.comment: An event involving the public showing of a movie or other video content. Also called film screening, movie showing, video presentation, cinema event. Examples: a film festival screening, a premiere showing of a new movie, a public documentary viewing, a drive-in movie night.

candidates.label: BankAccount
candidates.comment: A FinancialProduct or service offered by a bank for depositing, withdrawing, or transferring money, often with interest. Also called bank account, checking account, savings account, deposit account. Examples: "My personal checking account", "A business savings account", "A joint current account".

candidates.label: MonetaryAmount
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary value or range, typically expressed with a currency. Also called amount of money, financial value, currency amount. Examples: "$50 USD", "£1,000 to £1,000,000 GBP", "€25.99". Distinct from PriceSpecification, which describes the price of an offer.

candidates.label: EntertainmentBusiness
candidates.comment: An EntertainmentBusiness is a LocalBusiness that provides entertainment services. Also called amusement business, leisure provider. Examples: A movie theater, a concert venue, an arcade, a theme park.

types.oie_definition: A nation or state with its own government and borders.
types.embedding_query_text: Country: A nation or state with its own government and borders. Also called Nation, State, Territory.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: Continent
candidates.comment: One of the Earth's large landmasses, such as Europe or Africa. Also called major landmass, global region, land continent. Examples: Asia, North America, Antarctica, Australia. Distinct from Landform, which is a general term for a natural feature of the Earth's surface.

types.oie_definition: A period of 12 months, typically starting on January 1 and ending on December 31.
types.embedding_query_text: Year: A period of 12 months, typically starting on January 1 and ending on December 31. Also called Calendar Year, 12-Month Period, Annual Period.

chosen_type.label: Year
chosen_type.definition: A period of 12 months, typically starting on January 1 and ending on December 31.
chosen_type.justification: No existing type specifically represents a year

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

candidates.label: Periodical
candidates.comment: A Periodical, as a CreativeWorkSeries, is a publication issued in successive parts with numerical or chronological designations, intended to continue indefinitely. Also called serial publication, magazine, journal. Examples: The New Yorker magazine, a scholarly journal, a daily newspaper. Distinct from Book, which is a single, non-serial publication.

types.oie_definition: A person who performs in a movie, play, or other theatrical production.
types.embedding_query_text: Actor: A person who performs in a movie, play, or other theatrical production. Also called Actress, Performer, Thespian.

chosen_type.label: Actor
chosen_type.definition: A person who performs in a movie, play, or other theatrical production.
chosen_type.justification: No existing type specifically represents an actor

candidates.label: PerformanceRole
candidates.comment: A PerformanceRole, as a Role, is a role an entity plays in a theatrical performance, such as a movie or TV series. Also called acting role, character role, stage role. Examples: 'actor in a film', 'director of a play', 'musician in a concert'. Distinct from OrganizationRole, which is a role within an organization.

candidates.label: TheaterEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing a live performance in a theater. Also called stage play, theatrical show, drama performance. Examples: a Broadway musical, a local community play, a Shakespearean tragedy.

candidates.label: PerformingArtsTheater
candidates.comment: A PerformingArtsTheater is a civic structure or venue for performing arts. Also called theater, playhouse, concert hall. Examples: Sydney Opera House, a local community theater, a Broadway theater. Distinct from MovieTheater, which is for film screenings.

candidates.label: PerformAction
candidates.comment: A PerformAction, as a PlayAction, is the act of participating in performance arts. Also called act, perform, stage. Examples: performing in a play, playing a musical instrument on stage, dancing in a ballet. Distinct from PlayAction, which is a broader category for engaging in recreational activities.

candidates.label: Play
candidates.comment: A Play is a CreativeWork in the form of literature, primarily consisting of dialogue between characters, intended for theatrical performance. Also called stage play, drama, theatrical work. Examples: "Hamlet", "Death of a Salesman", "Hamilton", "A Streetcar Named Desire". Distinct from TheaterEvent, which is the actual performance of a play.

types.oie_definition: A female person who performs in a movie, play, or other theatrical production.
types.embedding_query_text: Actress: A female person who performs in a movie, play, or other theatrical production. Also called Female Actor, Performer, Theatrical Actress.
